03 / Vision

AI fluency is a leadership practice.

Tomorrow’s strongest teams will not simply use AI. They will know where it adds leverage, where human judgment must lead, and how to keep learning together.

I build capability, not dependency.

My role is to help people understand the tools, sharpen their judgment, and redesign how work moves—so AI expands what a team can do without eroding ownership, craft, or trust.

01
Context before tools

Start with the mission, the people, and the decision—not the latest model.

02
Develop people and systems together

Give teams shared language, practical standards, and room to build confidence.

03
Keep judgment human

Use AI to expand options and accelerate learning while people own the outcome.

04 / Leadership

Building tomorrow’s teams.

The work now extends beyond any one craft or industry: creating AI-fluent cultures, stronger leaders, and operating systems that help people adapt with purpose.

01

Applied AI fluency

I design and evaluate workflows using procedural generation, LLM-assisted review, in-game agents, and production automation—then translate the technology into language, decisions, and habits a whole team can use.

02

People leadership at scale

Leadership scale shown here: three international delivery teams led concurrently, alongside multi-studio internal artists, external vendors, and cross-functional partners. I align expectations, coach toward the quality bar, and make ownership clear.

03

Adaptive operating systems

I build the briefs, review paths, documentation, and feedback rhythms that keep distributed and live-service teams learning while they deliver—principles that transfer across professions and sectors.

The throughline is simple: give people the fluency, confidence, and systems to lead what comes next.
